rows.vgi.doc_md:
Every recurring series Polymarket lists, as an ordinary table — no argument required.

### What a series is, and is not

A series groups events that recur: `nfl` opens an event per game, and each of those events carries a market per outcome. Plenty of the biggest markets on the site are one-offs that belong to no series at all, so this is a view of the recurring part of Polymarket rather than of all of it — `tags` is the axis that covers everything.

### Where to go next

Take a `slug` and pass it to `events()` as `series_slug` for that series' occurrences.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Active recurring series by recent volume", "sql": "SELECT slug, title, recurrence, volume_24hr FROM polymarket.main.series WHERE active AND NOT closed ORDER BY volume_24hr DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20"}, {"description": "How many series run at each cadence", "sql": "SELECT recurrence, count(*) AS series_count FROM polymarket.main.series GROUP BY recurrence ORDER BY series_count DESC"}]
rows.vgi.title: Polymarket Recurring Series

rows: CREATE TABLE series(series_id VARCHAR, slug VARCHAR, ticker VARCHAR, title VARCHAR, description VARCHAR, series_type VARCHAR, recurrence VARCHAR, active BOOLEAN, closed BOOLEAN, archived BOOLEAN, featured BOOLEAN, volume_24hr DECIMAL(28,6), comment_count INTEGER, start_date TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, PRIMARY KEY(series_id));
Every topic on Polymarket; the tag_id everything else filters on

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The catalog of every topic on Polymarket — around 7,300 rows, small and slow-changing. This is the discovery entry point: `tag_id` is the filter `markets()` and `events()` both accept, and this is where you find one. Match on `label` or `slug` for a topic like Crypto, Politics or Sports.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Every topic tag Polymarket uses, as an ordinary table — no argument required.

### Why this is a table and most things are functions

It has no required key and changes slowly. The market-data functions are neither, which is why they take a key.

### The long tail is real

A few dozen tags carry nearly all the volume, and the rest are narrow one-off labels left over from individual events. Search `label` for the topic you want rather than browsing.

### Where to go next

Take a `tag_id` and pass it to `markets()` for the tradeable questions, or to `events()` for the groupings above them.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Find the tag id for a topic", "sql": "SELECT tag_id, label, slug FROM polymarket.main.tags WHERE label ILIKE '%crypto%' ORDER BY label"}, {"description": "Topics whose tags were published most recently", "sql": "SELECT label, slug, published_at FROM polymarket.main.tags WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY published_at DESC LIMIT 20"}]
rows.vgi.title: Polymarket Topic Tags

rows: CREATE TABLE tags(tag_id VARCHAR, "label" VARCHAR, slug VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, published_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, PRIMARY KEY(tag_id));
